chief_complaint: routine adolescent well-child exam, sports physical clearance, and preventive screening in 14-year-old male
hpi_details: 14-year-old boy presents accompanied by his mother for his annual adolescent well-child checkup and pre-participation sports physical examination prior to joining his high school soccer team. Reports feeling healthy with excellent exercise tolerance during running. Denies chest pain during exercise, shortness of breath, dizziness, or fainting during exertion. Family history is negative for sudden unexpected cardiac death before age 50 or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Mother notes he spends 4-5 hours daily playing video games and wants guidance on nutrition and vaccines.
ideas: excited to get cleared for high school soccer practice
concerns: mother wants to ensure his heart is safe for vigorous sports and update his immunizations
expectations: wants sports clearance form signed and guidance on teenage nutrition
pmh: Normal childhood history, fully vaccinated through age 11 (received Tdap and HPV dose 1 at age 11)

clinical_knowledge.topic: Adolescent Well-Child Exam and Sports Physical Clearance evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Adolescent Well-Child Exam and Sports Physical Clearance is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes sports clearance, immunization catch-up, and HEADSS-based anticipatory guidance, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: routine adolescent well-child exam, sports physical clearance, and preventive screening in 14-year-old male

Key HPI features: 14-year-old boy presents accompanied by his mother for his annual adolescent well-child checkup and pre-participation sports physical examination prior to joining his high school soccer team. Reports feeling healthy with excellent exercise tolerance during running. Denies chest pain during exercise, shortness of breath, dizziness, or fainting during exertion. Family history is negative for sudden unexpected cardiac death before age 50 or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Mother notes he spends 4-5 hours daily playing video games and wants guidance on nutrition and vaccines.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 68, BP 110/68 (normal for age/height percentile), RR 16, Height 168 cm (50th percentile), Weight 56 kg (50th percentile, BMI 19.8 kg/m2). Comprehensive PPE Physical Exam: 1. Cardiovascular exam: normal S1/S2, regular rhythm, no clicks. CRITICAL AUSCULTATION CHECK: Auscultation performed both in supine position and during active standing/Valsalva maneuver reveals NO systolic murmurs (specifically excluding the dynamic systolic murmur of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy which characteristically INCREASES in intensity during standing or Valsalva due to decreased venous return/left ventricular volume accentuating left ventricular outflow tract obstruction). Femoral pulses 2+ and symmetric bilaterally (excluding coarctation of the aorta). 2. Musculoskeletal exam: full 2-minute orthopedic screening exam shows normal spinal alignment (negative Adam's forward bend test for scoliosis), stable knees/ankles, and symmetric joint flexibility. 3. Genitourinary exam: normal Tanner Stage 4 development, bilateral descended testes without masses or inguinal hernia. Screening PHQ-9 Modified for Adolescents score: 1 (negative for depression).
Relevant background/PMH: Normal childhood history, fully vaccinated through age 11 (received Tdap and HPV dose 1 at age 11)
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Adolescent Well-Child Exam and Sports Physical Clearance.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Exertional chest pain, syncope, or a family history of sudden cardiac death before 50 — would require cardiology clearance before sports participation.
management_principles: Sports clearance: sign official Pre-participation Physical Examination (PPE) form clearing patient for full, unrestricted competitive high school soccer participation

Immunization administration: administer Quadrivalent Meningococcal Conjugate Vaccine booster (MenACWY / Menactra dose #1 is given at age 11-12; booster dose #2 recommended at age 16, or catch-up today if missed)
Verify completion of the 2-dose Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine series (if 2nd dose was not given 6-12 months after first dose at age 11, administer catch-up HPV dose #2 today)
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 14-year-old adolescent male presenting for annual preventive health maintenance and Pre-participation Physical Examination (PPE) for competitive high school soccer.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 68, BP 110/68 (normal for age/height percentile), RR 16, Height 168 cm (50th percentile), Weight 56 kg (50th percentile, BMI 19.8 kg/m2). Comprehensive PPE Physical Exam: 1. Cardiovascular exam: normal S1/S2, regular rhythm, no clicks. CRITICAL AUSCULTATION CHECK: Auscultation performed both in supine position and during active standing/Valsalva maneuver reveals NO systolic murmurs (specifically excluding the dynamic systolic murmur of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy which characteristically INCREASES in intensity during standing or Valsalva due to decreased venous return/left ventricular volume accentuating left ventricular outflow tract obstruction). Femoral pulses 2+ and symmetric bilaterally (excluding coarctation of the aorta). 2. Musculoskeletal exam: full 2-minute orthopedic screening exam shows normal spinal alignment (negative Adam's forward bend test for scoliosis), stable knees/ankles, and symmetric joint flexibility. 3. Genitourinary exam: normal Tanner Stage 4 development, bilateral descended testes without masses or inguinal hernia. Screening PHQ-9 Modified for Adolescents score: 1 (negative for depression).
reference_soap.assessment: Healthy 14-year-old adolescent male cleared for full participation in competitive sports without restrictions; due for routine adolescent immunization boosters.
reference_soap.plan: 1. Sports clearance: sign official Pre-participation Physical Examination (PPE) form clearing patient for full, unrestricted competitive high school soccer participation. 2. Immunization administration: verify MenACWY dose #1 was received at age 11-12 and schedule the routine booster at age 16; give a catch-up dose today only if the first dose was missed. Verify completion of the 2-dose Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine series (if dose #2 was not given 6-12 months after dose #1 at age 11, administer catch-up HPV dose #2 today). Administer annual Influenza vaccine. 3. Anticipatory guidance & HEADSS Counseling (Home, Education/Eating, Activities, Drugs, Sexuality, Suicide/Safety): counsel patient alone (with parent stepping out briefly) regarding dangers of vaping/e-cigarettes, alcohol, and energy drinks. Advise reducing recreational screen time to <2 hours daily, ensuring 8-10 hours of sleep nightly, and wearing seatbelts and bicycle/sports helmets.

learning_objectives: Perform a standardized Pre-participation Physical Examination (PPE) for adolescent athletes, focusing on cardiac red flags (personal history of exertional syncope/chest pain or family history of premature sudden cardiac death <age 50)

Execute specific cardiac auscultation maneuvers during sports physicals: auscultating while supine and during standing/Valsalva maneuvers to identify Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (whose systolic murmur uniquely louder upon standing/Valsalva due to decreased left ventricular preload increasing outflow tract obstruction)

Implement the CDC/ACIP adolescent immunization schedule including Tdap booster (age 11-12), Meningococcal conjugate vaccine MenACWY (dose 1 at 11-12, booster dose 2 at age 16), and Human Papillomavirus HPV vaccine (2-dose series if initiated before age 15)

Conduct structured adolescent psychosocial HEADSS screening (Home, Education, Activities, Drugs, Sexuality, Suicide/Mental Health) and provide confidential anticipatory guidance on vaping, nutrition, and injury prevention

teaching.diagnosis: Adolescent Well-Child Exam and Sports Physical Clearance
teaching.one_liner: A routine visit combining sports pre-participation screening (with special attention to cardiac red flags that could signal risk of sudden death) with catching up on adolescent immunizations and anticipatory guidance.
differentials: Occult cardiac disease with exertional symptoms
red_flags: Exertional chest pain, syncope, or a family history of sudden cardiac death before 50 — would require cardiology clearance before sports participation

must_ask.say: Have you ever had chest pain, dizziness, or fainting during exercise?
Has anyone in your family died suddenly at a young age, especially during sports?
Which vaccines has he already had, and are any due now?
How much time does he spend on screens, and how is his sleep?
(To the teen alone) Is there anything about drugs, alcohol, or how you're feeling that you'd like to talk about privately?

I want to be cleared to join the soccer team, and my mom wants advice on my diet and to make sure my shots are up to date.
I feel totally fine and don't have any pain, fever, or health issues right now.
No, I've never felt any chest pain, tightness, or pressure while running or playing soccer.
No, I don't get unusually out of breath when I sprint or exercise.
No, I have never passed out, blacked out, or felt lightheaded during or after exertion.
No, my heart beats fast when I play hard like anyone else, but it doesn't flutter or skip beats.
My stamina is great; I can run laps and keep up during practices without feeling worn out.
No, I've never had asthma, chest tightness, or coughing fits after running in the cold or exercising.
No, I've never had a concussion, head injury, or memory loss from sports.

No one in my family has died suddenly, unexpectedly, or drowned before age fifty.
No, nobody in our family has an enlarged heart muscle, heart attacks at an early age, or pacemakers.
I had all my childhood vaccines up to age eleven, including my Tdap and first HPV shot, but I might be due for boosters.
My last routine checkup was at age eleven before middle school, and the doctor said everything looked great.
I usually eat three meals a day, though I sometimes grab a quick muffin or cereal when rushing to morning classes.
I like chips and occasionally have soda or juice with friends, but I never drink energy drinks.
I spend about four to five hours playing video games on weekdays after homework, mostly online with classmates.
I get around six or seven hours of sleep on school nights because I tend to stay up late gaming.
My weight has been stable; I've just grown taller over the past year.
No, I have plenty of energy throughout the day and don't feel unusually cold or sluggish.
No, I don't snore or wake up choking or gasping during the night.
No, my knees, ankles, and back feel completely fine without any stiffness or swelling.
No, I don't feel constantly thirsty, and I don't have to get up at night to urinate.
I'm doing well emotionally; I'm excited about starting high school and haven't felt sad, depressed, or overwhelmed.
Home is safe and peaceful; I live with my mom, dad, and younger sister.
I'm a ninth grader and school is going well; I get mostly B's and some A's.
No, I don't smoke cigarettes, and I've never used vapes, e-cigarettes, or nicotine pouches.
No, I don't drink alcohol, and I have never tried marijuana or any illicit drugs.
No, I have not had sexual intercourse or any sexual activity.
I haven't had any chronic illnesses, seizures, or serious health problems.
None, I have never had an operation or stayed overnight in a hospital.
I don't take any prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, or sports supplements.
No, I have no known allergies to any medicines, foods, or materials.
My mom said I was born on my due date without any issues and walked and talked right on schedule.
My parents are both healthy in their early forties, with no history of diabetes, cancer, or high blood pressure.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 110/68 mmHg, heart rate 68 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 99% on room air, and body temperature 36.8°C.
Height 168 cm (50th percentile), weight 56 kg (50th percentile), and BMI 19.8 kg/m2, representing normal adolescent growth.
Regular rhythm with normal S1 and S2, no gallops or clicks, and no murmurs in the supine position or during standing and Valsalva maneuvers.
Bilateral femoral and radial pulses are 2+, brisk, and symmetric without radiofemoral delay.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally without wheezing, crackles, or signs of bronchospasm.
Normal spinal curvature and symmetric paraspinal contours on Adam's forward bend test without scoliosis or tenderness.
Full and symmetric range of motion in all major upper and lower extremity joints with stable knees and ankles.
Normal Tanner Stage 4 development with bilaterally descended testes and no scrotal masses or tenderness.
No visible or palpable inguinal hernia on cough impulse testing bilaterally.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, and smooth without palpable nodules or thyromegaly.
Warm, dry skin without purple striae, abnormal bruising, or acanthosis nigricans.
